newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco says future demand flat.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco says future demand flat.

text.p: Swedish engineering company Atlas Copco AB said on Thursday demand would be more or less unchanged in the near future.
It also said in a statement its 1997 profits would be somewhat higher than in 1996.
Atlas Copco posted an eight percent rise in profits after financial items of 3.07 billion crowns which was slightly above market expectations of a profit of 3.03 billion crowns.
"Demand in the near future is expected to remain largely unchanged," Atlas Copco said in a statement.
"Earnings for 1997 are expected to increase somewhat as a result of ongoing efficiency improvments."
Atlas Copco said its sales in 1996 rose three percent to 25.12 billion crowns even though the stronger Swedish crown had a negative impact of seven percent.
Markets outside Sweden accounted for 96 percent of invoicing.
Atlas Copco said higher demand was noted in North America, Southeast Asia, Australia and eastern Europe while sales developed negatively elsewhere in Europe including Germany, France and Britain.
Europe accounted for 43 percent of orders received in 1996 against 46 percent in 1995 while North American orders rose to 28 percent from 23 percent.
"Sales of large compressors, surface drill rigs, loaders and assembly systems improved," the company said
"Demand for power tools improved slightly during the second half of the year while sales of light construction equipment, such as portable compressors and breakers, declined."
The company said its profit margin rose to 12.2 percent from 11.6 percent a year earlier.
Profits included a gain of 342 million crowns related to the sale of VOAC Hydraulics and restructuring costs of 225 million in the industrial technique business area.
"Excluding these non-recurring items, the profit margin was 11.8 percent," the company said.
The company proposed a dividend of 3.75 crowns a share compared to 3.00 crowns in 1995.
After posting its result, Atlas Copco was trading 1.5 crowns higher at 175.5 crowns.
